title: Adaptive feature fusion for robust recognition under distribution shift
abstract: We study adaptive feature fusion for recognition under distribution shift. Adaptive fusion improves robustness on the source domain. Evaluation is limited to one dataset, leaving cross-domain behavior unverified.

title: On the limits of single-domain evaluation in adaptive models
abstract: Single-domain evaluation overestimates robustness of adaptive models. Adaptive fusion improves robustness on the training distribution, but evaluation is limited to one dataset and no parameter-matched cross-domain comparison exists.

title: Parameter-matched baselines for fair method comparison
abstract: Method comparisons are frequently confounded by parameter counts. We argue for parameter-matched baselines with multiple seeds. Adaptive fusion improves robustness in some regimes, but evaluation is limited to one dataset.

title: Calibration sets for distribution shift correction
abstract: Small calibration sets can correct covariate shift without full retraining. Evaluation is limited to one dataset and no parameter-matched comparison exists.

title: Seed variance in small-sample evaluation
abstract: Reported gains often disappear under multiple seeds. We recommend reporting seed-level variance. Adaptive fusion improves robustness claims rarely do this; evaluation is limited to one dataset.

title: Cross-domain benchmarks for adaptive models
abstract: A held-out multi-domain benchmark for adaptive models. No adaptive-fusion method has been evaluated on it under parameter-matched conditions; existing evaluation is limited to one dataset.
